summary: This work synthesizes high-fidelity quantum gates in superconducting linear chains by mapping periodic pulsed driving onto Floquet quasi-energy resonance conditions, achieving iSWAP gates in a three-qubit processor and demonstrating multi-excitation transport with $t_	ext{gate} 	hicksim 170$–430 ns in a seven-site architecture. Robustness analysis reveals sharp performance degradation under sub-percent static disorder ($	heta 	hicksim 10^{-3}$) in linear topologies, suggesting closed-loop ring geometries as a mitigation strategy.
motivation: Precise multi-qubit control remains a bottleneck in superconducting quantum processors; achieving high-fidelity entangling gates with durations much shorter than relaxation times ($T_1$, $T_//phi$) while maintaining scalability is essential for practical quantum computation.
method: Using Floquet theory, delta-kick pulses on flux-tunable transmon buses are mapped to quasi-energy resonance conditions via Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion; optimal driving parameters ($\lambda$, $T$, pulse amplitude $A$) are identified analytically and refined via Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES), with Gaussian pulse trains replacing idealized kicks for experimental feasibility.
result: Three-qubit iSWAP achieves fidelity $\mathcal{F} \approx 1.0$; seven-site double-excitation transfers reach $\mathcal{F} \gtrsim 0.99$ with ultra-short durations achieving $t_\text{gate}/T_1 \lesssim 2\%$, but fidelity collapses sharply for $\eta \gtrsim 10^{-3}$ parameter disorder due to spectral crowding in linear chains.
